about: Every number of the fiber-optic line, its strength, the spool it pays out of, the optical link it carries, the wires' end fittings, the launch layout, the span's nodes, the laid trail and the rotors' air on the line (p7d-tether design 1, 3, 4; PHY-18…21, D-024). The sim core reads it with DetJson through TetherTable, which refuses a missing block or field, an unknown one, a value without its label or rationale, a value of the wrong shape, and a derived value that does not equal its derivation from the table's own values. The flight log records every row and the file's hash; a replay refuses a tether.json of another hash. Randomness enters only through the bands and quantile tables named by design 14's streams (fiber.span_strength, fiber.section_strength, spool.peel, spool.irregularity, wire.strength, wire.tie), each drawn, bounded and logged; nothing about where the line lies is drawn. New values are added here by physics with the schema in TetherTable, never in code.

fields.value: a number; a band [lo, hi]; a vector [x, y, z] in the body frame (Unity's: +x right, +y up, +z forward), metres; or a quantile table [[p, value], …] with p rising from 0 to 1, read piecewise linearly
fields.label: where the number stands: pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed
fields.rationale: the source, the derivation or the reason

glass_diameter_m.label: published
glass_diameter_m.rationale: silica cladding Ø125 µm, ITU-T G.657 class (the drone sheet's 0.25 mm spool fiber, knowledge §5.1)

coating_diameter_m.label: published
coating_diameter_m.rationale: dual acrylate coating to Ø250 µm, ITU-T G.657 class; GetFPV's canister fiber is 0.26 mm

coating_thickness_m.label: derived
coating_thickness_m.rationale: (coating − glass diameter)/2; the depth abrasion must wear through before the glass is touched (design 7)

mass_per_m_kg.label: derived
mass_per_m_kg.rationale: 0.069 kg/km: drone.json's coil, 0.69 kg of line over 10 000 m (glass at 2.2 g/cm³ plus coating at about 1.15 g/cm³)

weight_per_m_n.label: derived
weight_per_m_n.rationale: mass_per_m_kg times the core's g, 9.80665 m/s²

glass_area_m2.label: derived
glass_area_m2.rationale: π·d²/4 of the glass; the coating carries under 1 % of the axial load and is left out (design 1)

axial_stiffness_n.label: derived
axial_stiffness_n.rationale: EA of the glass, E·A_g: the cable chain's segment spring EA/ℓ₀ (design 2)

bending_stiffness_n_m2.label: derived
bending_stiffness_n_m2.rationale: EI of the glass, E·π·d⁴/64 (the coating adds under 15 %, left out): the elastica's bend length √(EI/T) at every contact, the lip and the peel point (design 6, 7)

proof_stress_pa.label: published
proof_stress_pa.rationale: the 100 kpsi screen every length is proof-tested to (Telcordia GR-20, TIA FOTP-31): no flaw below it survives the factory

proof_force_n.label: derived
proof_force_n.rationale: proof_stress_pa times the glass area: the tension at which a span is as weak as it can be

coating_modulus_pa.label: assumed
coating_modulus_pa.rationale: the cured acrylate's modulus for the Hertz pressure of the line on an edge (the fortifications reading §2.4)

coating_poisson_ratio.label: assumed
coating_poisson_ratio.rationale: the acrylate's Poisson ratio for the same Hertz contact (the fortifications reading §2.4)

coating_hardness_pa.label: assumed
coating_hardness_pa.rationale: Archard's H: the geometric mean of the acrylate's 0.05–0.1 GPa (the fortifications reading §2.4); the acceptance harness prints the targets' sensitivity across that band (design 16)

archard_wear_coefficient.label: assumed
archard_wear_coefficient.rationale: Archard's k on an abrasive member (a barb, razor tape, a sheared or rolled metal arris of 1 mm or less, a rough row: bark, concrete, masonry): the geometric mean of 0.01–0.05 (the fortifications reading §2.4), the two-body abrasion band, so 18–88 loaded rubs of one section wear through the coating; the harness prints the sensitivity across that band

archard_wear_coefficient_mild.label: assumed
archard_wear_coefficient_mild.rationale: Archard's k on a smooth member (the drone's carbon, aluminium and polymer parts, a conductor, a smooth face whose arris is over 1 mm): the mild-wear band of polymers sliding on smooth metal, 1e-6–1e-4 (published, Archard and Hirst 1956; Hutchings, Tribology, 1992), its middle in decades (p7d-tether 1.8: the severe band on a smooth part wore the coating through in millimetres of sliding)

section_length_m.label: assumed
section_length_m.rationale: the length each per-section draw covers (fiber.section_strength, spool.irregularity), indexed by the material coordinate s so the order of use never shifts a draw (design 7, 14); the props' scale near the exit

drag_cross_base.label: published
drag_cross_base.rationale: C_d = base + coefficient·Re^exponent across a circular cylinder, 1 < Re < 2·10⁵ (White, Viscous Fluid Flow, 3rd ed.); a falling line settles at 1.4 m/s, Re 24 (derived, design 3)

drag_cross_reynolds.label: published
drag_cross_reynolds.rationale: the Reynolds numbers White's fit holds over

drag_axial.label: assumed
drag_axial.rationale: skin friction along the line on its surface area (design 1)

air_kinematic_viscosity_m2_s.label: published
air_kinematic_viscosity_m2_s.rationale: ISA sea level at 15 °C: μ 1.789e-5 Pa·s over ρ 1.225 kg/m³; the line's Reynolds number v·d/ν

wet_film_rain_m.label: assumed
wet_film_rain_m.rationale: the water film a line carries in Rain (D-021, design 5): 0.35 mm across and 68 % heavier

air_density_kg_m3.label: published
air_density_kg_m3.rationale: ISA sea level at 15 °C: the line's drag ½ρu² and the rotors' induced velocity √(T/2ρA) at the line (design 3, 4); air_kinematic_viscosity_m2_s is μ over this

span_pa.label: assumed
span_pa.rationale: fiber.span_strength, one draw per flight at arming, met by T/A_g anywhere on the span (design 7): the floor is the proof stress (published); the ceiling is assumed, a fifth of a short section's, because a whole span breaks near its proof-truncated weakest flaw (Weibull's weakest link, published); uniform inside, the shape assumed: 8.5–17 N

flaw_spacing_m.label: assumed
flaw_spacing_m.rationale: one surviving flaw per 20 km of line: a section holds one with probability section_length_m/flaw_spacing_m (design 7); tied to the fact that a 10 km canister pays out at cruise safely on all but rare flights (design 16, published)

flaw_pa.label: assumed
flaw_pa.rationale: a flawed section's local strength, from the proof stress (published floor) to the intact floor; uniform inside (assumed)

intact_pa.label: assumed
intact_pa.rationale: an intact section's local strength at a bend, under the published means of 4.5–5.5 GPa in short-gauge tension and 6.5–7.6 GPa in bending (the fortifications reading's sources); uniform inside (assumed)

abraded_pa.label: assumed
abraded_pa.rationale: a section worn through its coating, redrawn on the same counter (design 7): abraded glass, Weibull modulus 3–7 against 30–100 for pristine fiber (published); uniform inside (assumed)

peel_energy_j_m.label: derived
peel_energy_j_m.rationale: spool.peel, G₀ drawn per flight from this quantile table: the published peel forces of fiber canister packs (US 5,167,382 and its cited art), 0.01–2 g for a lightly bonded pack (which also pays out satisfactorily with no adhesive) and 5–10 g for a conventionally bonded one, read at a 90° test angle, G = F·(1 − cos 90°) = F; the light band on half the flights and 2–10 g on the other half (the split assumed: the patent gives the two as alternatives, and drone sellers write 'near zero'; p7d-tether design 18, docs/reference-notes/fiber-exit.md §5.3). Models to 88 drew 2–10 g uniformly

peel_rate_exponent.label: assumed
peel_rate_exponent.rationale: G = G₀·max(1, (ṡ/v_ref)^n): within the published 0.1–0.3 exponents of rubbery adhesives' peel energy (Gent and Petrich 1969)

peel_reference_rate_m_s.label: published
peel_reference_rate_m_s.rationale: v_ref of the peel's rate law, the payout rate at which the band's peel force is the published one: the 5–10 g of a conventionally bonded pack, and the 2 g or less of a lightly bonded one, are forces during payout (US 5,167,382) of canisters for missiles flying at 100 m/s and more, tested to about 300 m/s; under it G is held at G₀ (a rate-dependent adhesive's G only falls with the rate, Gent and Petrich 1969: the held G₀ is its upper bound, conservative for the cut). At model 56–73's 1 m/s, G₀ grew by (ṡ/1 m/s)^0.2, 1.72× at 15 m/s, and the peel front bent the glass 3.0–3.2 GPa in cruise on high-peel seeds, cutting cruising lines, which the pilot's 80–100 km/h contradicts (D-087); now at most E·r·√(2·G₀·1.25/EI) = 2.41 GPa, under the intact band's 3.0 GPa floor, at any speed under 100 m/s (derived)

irregularity.label: assumed
irregularity.rationale: spool.irregularity, the pack's resistance factor per section (±25 %): the adhesive's spread and the winding's cross-overs

balloon_length_m.label: assumed
balloon_length_m.rationale: L_b, the line between the peel point and the exit whose acceleration the exit tension carries (μ·L_b·s̈, design 3; the FOG-M review's friction-and-adhesive term plus ρv², published)

lip_radius_m.label: assumed
lip_radius_m.rationale: the hole's edge the line leaves over (D-087: it tears upon the canister hole's edge): the bore's arris at the class's outlet, an aluminium-alloy nozzle (GetFPV's 10 km canister, published) or a high-hardness ceramic outlet (a 15 km spool's listing, published), or a bare moulded or printed hole in the shell, which the line grooves (Glory Optics, a vendor's account: the exit port is a localized bending and wear point, published); no published edge radius (docs/reference-notes/spool-exit-and-rear.md §6): a broken edge of 0.3 mm. The bend there is the larger of R_edge + c and the elastica's √(EI/T)/(2·sin(θ/4)) (FiberCuts); the elastica's is the larger at every tension under EI/(2·sin(θ/4)·(R_edge + c))², for a 0.5 mm edge 1.4 N at a 180° wrap and 4.7 N at 90°, so any edge under 0.5 mm gives the same stress at the exit's tensions, E·r·2·sin(θ/4)·√(T/EI) + T/A_g: 3.0 GPa, the intact band's floor, at 0.19 N round 180°, 0.38 N round 120° and 0.65 N round 90° (derived). Model 64–73's 4 mm flared lip (assumed) held the glass under 1.2 GPa plus T/A_g, so it could never tear there

lip_archard_wear_coefficient.label: assumed
lip_archard_wear_coefficient.rationale: Archard's k of the coating on the hole's edge (FiberCuts.WearLip): the mild band of fiber.archard_wear_coefficient_mild, as the class's outlets are finished for a smooth payout, an aluminium-alloy nozzle (GetFPV, published) or a polished high-hardness ceramic insert (published listings); a bare plastic hole the line has grooved and cracked (Glory Optics' account) takes the severe band, fiber.archard_wear_coefficient, which the turn grid flies as the known-wrong

mouth_radius_m.label: derived
mouth_radius_m.rationale: the hole's radius: D01's nozzle, an Ø18 mm aluminium tube with a 3 mm wall, its bore Ø12 mm (drone.json's canister mass note, D01_*.json's bore_d_m): the line pressed on the hole's edge slides round it by this radius times its lead's turn about the nozzle's axis (FiberCuts.WearLip)

nozzle_length_m.label: derived
nozzle_length_m.rationale: the tube the line runs through to the hole: drone.json's 0.070 m nozzle (its canister's length note: about 70 mm, published [3]; the builds' 0.06–0.08 m, measured); the line can lie across the bore and leave up to atan(2·mouth_radius_m/nozzle_length_m) = 9.7° off the nozzle's axis without touching the hole's edge (derived), so the edge wears it only beyond that (FiberCuts.WearLip)

lip_friction.label: derived
lip_friction.rationale: μ of the coating on the nozzle: the median of the 11 published values of a cured acrylate coating film on stainless steel, band 0.36–1.0 (published, US 6,362,249 B2 Tables 2–3; docs/reference-notes/fiber-exit.md §2.1), steel standing in for the aluminium nozzle as the coating's own shear sets μ on a hard smooth face (assumed), constant with load (Amontons: the contact is near fully plastic, §2.2). It enters design 18's point-contact law at the bore's entry and the hole's edge (T₂/T₁ 1.26 at 30°, 1.87 at 90°, 2.33 at 150°, 2.39 at 180°, under the capstan's e^(μθ) 1.27, 2.03, 3.25, 4.11) and the capstan only where the line wraps the edge. Models to 88: 0.3, assumed, below every published coating-on-steel value

exit_position_m.label: derived
exit_position_m.rationale: the nozzle's tip, where the line leaves the canister through its hole: drone.json's coil_nozzle contact's aft core end plus its 0.013 m radius down the nozzle's own axis, 0.070 m from the cone's collar (drone.json's canister at (0, −0.109, 0.023) on its 15° axis, the nozzle bent 12.5° below it at the collar); 0.040 m aft of the rear motors' axis and 0.184 m below the arm plane, inside the class's measured 0.03–0.08 m and 0.12–0.20 m (docs/reference-notes/spool-exit-and-rear.md §2.2), 0.069 m above level ground on the legs. Model 64–73: (0, −0.170081, −0.204958), the nozzle straight on the canister's 15°

exit_direction.label: derived
exit_direction.rationale: the nozzle's axis out of the tip, aft and 27.5° down, derived from the pilot's angle: D-086, the spool is mounted so the fiber leaves its hole at about 25–30°, so a climb or a throttle-up shares the pull with the angle instead of dragging the fiber across the hole's edge; the band's middle (nothing in the physics or the airframe picks a narrower value: with the sim's drag the nose is down 27.5° at about 77 km/h, where the nozzle then points straight aft: 24.0° at 72 km/h, 37.8° at 90, p7d-tether 1.8's grid). The canister stays at its 15° and the nozzle is bent 12.5° at its collar (drone.json's coil_nozzle: the canister tilted to 27.5° would leave its cone 3 mm off level ground); models 64–73 flew the class's photos' 15° (7–20°, §2.2–2.3). The lip's wrap θ_e is measured from it, and the launch lays the line from the tip along it to the ground, as the class's builds rest (§2.3, §4); a unit vector, the coil_nozzle capsule's own axis

wavelength_m.label: assumed
wavelength_m.rationale: the video downlink of a bidirectional pair at 1550 nm

budget_db.label: assumed
budget_db.rationale: launch power over receiver sensitivity: the low end of the published 20 km BiDi SFP class (−8…−3 dBm out, −23 dBm sensitivity)

connector_loss_db.label: assumed
connector_loss_db.rationale: connectors and splices at the station and the drone

launch_margin_db.label: derived
launch_margin_db.rationale: budget_db less connector_loss_db: the margin with no line paid out and no bend

attenuation_db_per_m.label: published
attenuation_db_per_m.rationale: 0.21 dB/km, typical of G.657 at 1550 nm (ITU's maximum is 0.30)

macrobend_loss_a_db.label: published
macrobend_loss_a_db.rationale: ITU-T G.657.A2's limit for one turn at 7.5 mm radius, 1550 nm; the law L(R) = L_a·e^(−decay·(R − R_a)) per full turn passes through it; limits are maxima, so the law is the worst compliant fiber's (assumed)

macrobend_loss_b_db.label: published
macrobend_loss_b_db.rationale: ITU-T G.657.A2's limit for one turn at 10 mm radius, 1550 nm

macrobend_decay_per_m.label: derived
macrobend_decay_per_m.rationale: ln(L_a/L_b)/(R_b − R_a) = ln 5/2.5 mm: 2.5 dB a turn at 5 mm, 9.1 at 3 mm, 17.2 at 2 mm

microbend_smooth_db_per_n.label: assumed
microbend_smooth_db_per_n.rationale: c_m, the microbend loss per newton pressing the line on a smooth contact (metal, polymer, the drone's parts, a conductor): the order of the sandpaper-drum test of IEC TR 62221 (15–20 N/m on fine abrasive gives well under 1 dB/km on a bend-insensitive fiber), so a contact's loss is a few thousandths of a dB beside a bend's (design 8)

microbend_rough_db_per_n.label: assumed
microbend_rough_db_per_n.rationale: c_m on a rough contact (soil, bark, concrete, straw, fabric): a hundred times the smooth one for millimetre-scale roughness

dip_threshold_db.label: assumed
dip_threshold_db.rationale: the receiver loses the picture when the margin falls below 0 dB (design 8)

dip_hysteresis_db.label: assumed
dip_hysteresis_db.rationale: a dip ends when the margin is back above threshold plus this

tie_hold_n.label: assumed
tie_hold_n.rationale: wire.tie for a bare conductor's tie on a hook or pin: the pull it holds before slipping, of the order of 10–25 % of the conductor's rated strength

tie_unseat_slip_m.label: assumed
tie_unseat_slip_m.rationale: the slip after which a tie leaves its seat and the span drops

sip_clamp_hold_ratio.label: assumed
sip_clamp_hold_ratio.rationale: a SIP anchor clamp holds its conductor's rated strength

house_anchor_hold_n.label: assumed
house_anchor_hold_n.rationale: wire.tie for a service drop's house anchor: its pull-out force

conductor_strength_ratio.label: assumed
conductor_strength_ratio.rationale: wire.strength, each conductor's breaking force as a factor of its record's: the ГОСТ figure is a minimum, and old conductors corrode

anchor_behind_start_m.label: assumed
anchor_behind_start_m.rationale: the line's far end at the ground station on the ground, 3 m behind the start point; the line laid straight from it to where the nozzle's lead (spool.exit_direction) meets the ground, beneath the exit for a level one (the pilot sets the drone down on its line)

max_nodes.label: assumed
max_nodes.rationale: the active chain from the touchdown to the exit (design 3, PHY-18's ≤ 32 lumped nodes): near_spacing_m within near_length_m of the exit and spacing_growth a node beyond cover about 1.5 km of line, more than any airborne arc

near_spacing_m.label: assumed
near_spacing_m.rationale: a segment's rest length within near_length_m of the exit: the props' and the legs' scale, where the line meets the drone's own air and parts (design 3)

near_length_m.label: assumed
near_length_m.rationale: the line from the exit, material metres, spaced at near_spacing_m (design 3)

spacing_growth.label: assumed
spacing_growth.rationale: beyond near_length_m each segment's rest length is this many times the one before (design 3): the rest length grows by spacing_growth − 1 per material metre

ground_reach_m.label: assumed
ground_reach_m.rationale: a node this close to the ground takes the ground as a contact (design 6, 12); 1.7: within it the plane (where the world has one; over a hole the shapes there are the ground)

ground_static_friction.label: assumed
ground_static_friction.rationale: μs of the line's acrylate coating on the ground: drone.json's polymer pair on the ground's surfaces (the coating as a polymer part, design 1); since 1.7 the plane and a soil shape take their surface's own (surfaces.json's set at the flight's moisture), and this pair is the fallback without surfaces.json and the μ on the drone's polymer parts

ground_kinetic_friction.label: assumed
ground_kinetic_friction.rationale: μk of the same pair (drone.json's ground_friction_kinetic)

coil_rebuild_m.label: assumed
coil_rebuild_m.rationale: the mass model, the inertia and the airframe's coil mode are rebuilt each time this much line has paid out (0.69 g of line, design 3), the body's motion kept

freeze_seconds.label: assumed
freeze_seconds.rationale: a node resting on the ground this long, slower than freeze_speed_m_s and held by its friction, is frozen into the laid trail (design 3)

freeze_speed_m_s.label: assumed
freeze_speed_m_s.rationale: the speed under which a node on the ground counts as resting (design 3)

capacity.label: assumed
capacity.rationale: the laid trail's points, preallocated: 10 km of line at 0.6 m a point (design 3); an overflow merges the oldest pair and logs a WorldBug

hold_length_m.label: assumed
hold_length_m.rationale: the laid line whose friction holds the trail's last point: it lifts back into the chain when the tension at the touchdown, or the rotors' air on it, passes μs times the weight of this much line (design 3)

far_wake_speed_ratio.label: published
far_wake_speed_ratio.rationale: the wake below a disc moves at twice the induced velocity (momentum theory's far wake; Johnson 1980, Leishman 2006), design 4

far_wake_radius_ratio.label: published
far_wake_radius_ratio.rationale: the far wake contracts to R/√2 (momentum theory's continuity at 2v_i; Leishman 2006), design 4

wake_reach_over_radius.label: assumed
wake_reach_over_radius.rationale: the known-wrong since design 19 (FlightSetup.TetherWakeReach4R; the law is the merged jet's landing from any height): the wake column reaches the ground and turns into the radial wall jet when the disc is within this many radii of it, measured along the wake: about two diameters before a hover wake mixes out (design 4 assumed 2R; drone.json's legs-on disc stands 2.27R up, so 2R would leave the liftoff without its jet)

wall_jet_thickness_over_radius.label: derived
wall_jet_thickness_over_radius.rationale: h_j where the column turns: its flux π(R/√2)²·2v_i leaves through 2π(R/√2)·h_j at the column's own speed, so h_j = far_wake_radius_ratio·R/2 (mass conservation; design 4's assumed 0.1R would make the jet 3.5 times faster than the column it comes from); beyond, u = πR²v_i/(2π·r·h_j)

wall_lift_coefficient.label: published
wall_lift_coefficient.rationale: a circular cylinder resting on a plane wall in a cross-flow is lifted off it, C_L ≈ 0.9 on the wall in a steady current (the pipeline on the seabed: Sumer and Fredsøe, Hydrodynamics Around Cylindrical Structures, 2006; DNV-RP-F109): the wall jet lifts a line lying in it (design 4)

wall_lift_gap_over_diameter.label: assumed
wall_lift_gap_over_diameter.rationale: the wall lift falls linearly to zero as the gap under the line reaches this many diameters (the published curves fall to small values at a gap of 0.5–1 diameters)

fountain_momentum_ratio.label: derived
fountain_momentum_ratio.rationale: the fountain's momentum over the colliding wall jets' normal momentum (p7d 1.6b, D-075): the plane jet so built reaches 3R on the midline at w = 0.25·w_ind between two rotors one diameter apart tip to tip at H/R 4, as measured (Dekker, Baars, Scarano, Tuinstra, Ragni, Unsteady flow behaviour of multi-rotors in ground proximity, Flow 3 E30, 2023: R 76.2 mm, 2.14 N, w_ind 14.25 m/s; RotorAirTests); 0.29 of the jets' momentum lost where they meet

plane_jet_spreading_rate.label: published
plane_jet_spreading_rate.rationale: the self-similar plane jet's half-width growth db/dy (Pope, Turbulent Flows, 2000, §5.4; Bradbury 1965, J. Fluid Mech. 23): the fountain rises as a plane jet, self-similar as the twin-jet fountains measured (Saddington, Knowles, Cabrita, Aeronautical J. 113, 2009); with the Gaussian profile it gives U_j²/w_c² = 0.151·y/b_slot, its spread 0.66 of that, as measured (≈ 0.6, Mi and Feng, Chin. Phys. B 20, 2011)

fountain_impingement_depth_ratio.label: published
fountain_impingement_depth_ratio.rationale: the depth below a body's underside over which the fountain's plane jet stagnates, over the jet's length from its virtual origin to the underside (p7d-tether, model 61): plane turbulent impinging jets behave as free plane jets to 70-75 % of the jet's height, then turn at the wall (Khayrullina, van Hooff, Blocken, van Heijst, Experiments in Fluids 58:31, 2017, PIV at 22.5 and 45 slot widths), the band's middle; under a body narrower than the jet its own stagnation depth governs (RotorAir: a/2 under a cylinder, a/3 under a sphere, the potential flow's slope at the stagnation point, Batchelor 1967)

body_lee_length_over_diameter.label: assumed
body_lee_length_over_diameter.rationale: the length over a part's top, in its diameters, of the separated near wake in which the fountain's mean rise is taken as nothing (p7d-tether, model 61): the mean recirculation bubble behind a circular cylinder is about 1.5 D at Re 3900 (Parnaudeau, Carlier, Heitz, Lamballais, Phys. Fluids 20, 085101, 2008) and shorter at the coil's Re of about 4e4 (7 m/s over 83 mm); 1 D taken; the coil's lee up to the discs' plane is 0.55 D, so the flow the line meets there is the same for any length from 0.55 D up

hover_like_advance_ratio.label: published
hover_like_advance_ratio.rationale: μ* = U/v_h up to which the flow under a rotor near the ground stays hover-like, a small recirculation far ahead (Wolf, Weiss, Schwarz, Braukmann, Koch, Raffel, J. AHS 67, 012010, 2022, after Sheridan and Wiesner 1977 and Curtiss et al. 1984): the fountain whole up to it, then fading; the ground vortex growing from nothing at hover to its whole at it (the ramps assumed)

ground_vortex_advance_ratio.label: published
ground_vortex_advance_ratio.rationale: the ground vortex stands up to μ* 0.9 and is gone by the flight test's 1.19 (Wolf et al. 2022, after Sheridan and Wiesner 1977 and Curtiss et al. 1984): the vortex fades over the band (linear, assumed), and the fountain has faded out at its start (the flow ahead OGE-like beyond it)

ground_vortex_offset_over_radius.label: derived
ground_vortex_offset_over_radius.rationale: the vortex's centre ahead of the wake's landing point is offset·R + penetration·r_p, r_p = R²·v_i/(2·h_j·U) where the wall jet meets the stream: the two through Wolf et al. 2022's full-scale centres (Bo105, hub at 0.96–1.02 R, the speed's peak at y/R 0.19) 1.07 R ahead of the hub at μ* 0.55 and 0.49 R at 0.80, on this field's landing and jet (RotorAirTests); at μ* 0.7–0.9 the centre is then under the disc, 0.71–0.27 R ahead of the hub, as published

ground_vortex_penetration_ratio.label: derived
ground_vortex_penetration_ratio.rationale: see ground_vortex_offset_over_radius: the share of the wall jet's penetration r_p in the vortex's distance ahead of the landing point, from the same two measured centres

ground_vortex_height_over_jet.label: assumed
ground_vortex_height_over_jet.rationale: the vortex's centre stands the wall jet's thickness h_j above the ground: the separated jet rolls up within its own depth

ground_vortex_core_over_height.label: assumed
ground_vortex_core_over_height.rationale: the vortex's Scully core radius over its height: the core reaches halfway to the ground

ground_vortex_circulation.label: derived
ground_vortex_circulation.rationale: Γ/(v_h·R): with the vortex so placed, its image under the ground and the wall jet, the speed at y/R 0.19 under the centre is 1.59 v_h at μ* 0.55 and 1.65 v_h at 0.80 against Wolf et al. 2022's measured 1.5 and 1.75 (least squares in the log, RotorAirTests)

ground_vortex_half_span_over_radius.label: assumed
ground_vortex_half_span_over_radius.rationale: each rotor's vortex spans its wake's width, R either side of the centre, a straight vortex across the stream (the horseshoe's legs left out); a rotor whose upstream jet meets another's landing within one span across forms none, ramped to two spans across and over one along

wake_merge_over_motor_distance.label: published
wake_merge_over_motor_distance.rationale: the four rotors' jets converge about one motor distance l below the rotors and have merged into one turbulent round jet by about 2.5 l (Bauersfeld, Muller, Ziegler, Coletti, Scaramuzza, IEEE RA-L 2024, arXiv 2403.13321: six quadrotors 0.23-6.3 kg, 1.5-2.5 l over them); between, the near columns and the merged jet are blended linearly (assumed), design 19

far_jet_decay.label: published
far_jet_decay.rationale: the merged jet's centreline U_C = U_H·Bd/(s/l - s0/l), Bd = 10.11 (Bauersfeld et al. 2024, eq. 9, fitted over the uncanted drones), U_H the rotors' rms induced velocity, l the motor distance (diagonal wheelbase), design 19

far_jet_spreading_rate.label: published
far_jet_spreading_rate.rationale: the merged jet's half-width r½ = S·(s/l - s0/l)·l, S = 0.07668, with the profile U = U_C/(1 + (√2 - 1)ξ²)², ξ = r/r½ (Bauersfeld et al. 2024, eqs. 3, 6, 9), design 19

far_jet_virtual_origin_over_motor_distan.label: published
far_jet_virtual_origin_over_motor_distan.rationale: the merged jet's virtual origin s0/l = -5.817 (above the rotors; Bauersfeld et al. 2024, eq. 9), design 19

wall_jet_half_height_ratio.label: published
wall_jet_half_height_ratio.rationale: the radial wall jet's outer half-height δ = 0.098·r·(r/H)^-0.1 under a normally impinging round jet, H the wall's distance from the jet's origin (Poreh, Tsuei, Cermak, J. Appl. Mech. 34, 1967, as tabulated in Phys. Fluids 29, 025102, 2017), design 19

wall_jet_half_height_exponent.label: published
wall_jet_half_height_exponent.rationale: the exponent of (r/H) in the wall jet's half-height over r (Poreh et al. 1967), design 19

wall_jet_decay_exponent.label: published
wall_jet_decay_exponent.rationale: the radial wall jet's maximum velocity falls as r^-1.1 (Poreh et al. 1967; 'a universal constant close to -1.1' above a critical Reynolds number, Phys. Fluids 29, 025102, 2017): momentum's r^-1 and the wall's friction, design 19

wall_jet_profile.label: published
wall_jet_profile.rationale: Verhoff's (1963) wall jet profile u/u_m = b·η^(1/7)·(1 - erf(a·η)), η = y/δ, [a, b] = [0.68, 1.48] (as compared with Poreh's and others' data in Mahoney et al., A Colebrook equation for impinging radial wall jets, PNNL, OSTI 2587227); f(1) = 0.498 and its peak 1.000 at η 0.165 (derived: the constants read right), design 19

wall_jet_profile_square_integral.label: derived
wall_jet_profile_square_integral.rationale: ∫₀^∞ f(η)² dη of Verhoff's profile (numerical quadrature; RotorAirTests checks it): with the momentum flux of the landing jet it sets r_i, where the wall jet begins, r_i = r½/√(6(√2 - 1)·c_i·∫f²), design 19

clearance_margin_m.label: assumed
clearance_margin_m.rationale: the clearance certificate's margin (design 12): a swept query of a segment against the world's shapes that finds nothing within this certifies it clear until either end has moved this less the line's radius, so a line hanging in the open at 20 m/s is queried about once in 25 steps; a segment in contact or within the margin of a shape is queried every step

drone_cache_radius_m.label: assumed
drone_cache_radius_m.rationale: the elements, snag records and conductors around the drone the line's segments are tested against each step (design 12): p7a-ground design 8's 2 m cache of the drone, carried

drone_cache_refresh_m.label: assumed
drone_cache_refresh_m.rationale: the drone's cache is asked for again once the drone is this far from its centre (p7a-ground design 8's, carried): with the 20-step swap it holds to about 50 m/s

line_cache_radius_m.label: assumed
line_cache_radius_m.rationale: each of the two caches at the line's lowest touching nodes (design 12, the surfaces review §6.1): where the line lies far from the drone, on a mat or in a crown

line_cache_refresh_m.label: assumed
line_cache_refresh_m.rationale: a line cache is asked for again once its node is this far from its centre: a quarter of its radius, as the drone's 0.5 of 2 m

cache_swap_steps.label: assumed
cache_swap_steps.rationale: a cache asked for in a step is used from this many steps later, never when the worker is done (api-review §6), so a replay swaps at the same step with the same bits

element_capacity.label: assumed
element_capacity.rationale: a cache's elements, preallocated: p7a-ground design 8's 8192, about twice S04's density over the 2 m disc (4527 at r 2 m, p7a 1.9); overflow is a WorldBug and the canonical prefix is used

snag_capacity.label: assumed
snag_capacity.rationale: a cache's snag record segments, preallocated: twice the map compiler's 2048 in any 2 m cube (the fortifications reading §7); V01_L's whole crown holds 820 within 12 m; overflow is a WorldBug and the canonical prefix is used

wire_capacity.label: assumed
wire_capacity.rationale: a cache's conductors (design 13's eight active conductors); overflow is a WorldBug and the canonical prefix is used

stem_slide_off_share.label: assumed
stem_slide_off_share.rationale: a standing stem lets the line slide off its tip once pushed this share of the contact's height across (p7a-ground design 8's stems, carried)

hook_reach_m.label: assumed
hook_reach_m.rationale: a hooked straw's spring reaches its release force over this pull (p7a-ground design 8's hooks, carried)

aluminium_static_friction.label: assumed
aluminium_static_friction.rationale: μs of the coating on the motors' aluminium cans: the steel row's of physics_materials.json, the nearest metal there (no aluminium row: the cans are the drone's, design 6)

aluminium_kinetic_friction.label: assumed
aluminium_kinetic_friction.rationale: μk of the same pair (the steel row's)
